title: One cable; two different terminations
bullets: Coax enters the atmospheric tube directly
Outer shield bonds to grounded Boden
Insulated center reaches the live Backplate
speech: Here is the simpler proposal with one continuous coax cable. It enters through the atmospheric service tube. There is no additional S M A connector on the gun. The blue gray path is the grounded shield and structure. The orange path is the R F center conductor and live cathode assembly. The cream colored material provides electrical insulation. The two coolant hoses are hidden so we can inspect the electrical terminations.

title: Ground connection: shield to Boden
bullets: Short, wide strap to the grounded bottom body
New blind anchor stays inside the dry cavity
speech: At the grounded bottom body, expose a short section of the cable shield and capture it with a circumferential conductive clamp. A short, wide metal strap bonds that clamp to the inner surface of the grounded Boden. The proposed anchor is blind and stays inside the dry cavity; its final depth and position must be checked against the original holes and sealing surfaces. This is the shield connection. It does not attach to the live spacer or copper head.

title: RF connection: center to copper terminal
bullets: Shield ends on the grounded side
Inner dielectric protects the continuing center
Ring lug connects at the separate live M4 terminal
speech: The center conductor continues beyond the shield termination with its dielectric protection intact. It curves through the open central space to the existing live terminal on the copper Backplate. A secure ring lug replaces a loose wire hook at that terminal. Only the short terminal connection is exposed. The main P T F E ring separates the live spacer from the grounded bottom body. This is a proposed mechanical route; conductor protection, R F voltage clearance and cable ratings still need final design.
